drills.title: Contain It: Bio & Rad Decisions
drills.description: PPE, risk, and the right move for invisible threats. Wrong call = exposed crew or delayed care.

items.prompt: Suspected smallpox patient. Your respiratory protection?

items.why: Pneumonic plague spreads by respiratory droplets.

items.prompt: Patient exposed to a hidden radiation source, no contamination. Risk to you?
items.why: Exposure doesn't make a person radioactive.

items.prompt: Contaminated dirty-bomb victim with arterial bleeding.
items.why: Life threats first. Radiological contamination is rarely immediately dangerous.

items.prompt: Best first decon step for radiological contamination?
You move from 1 m to 2 m from a source. Your dose rate becomes…

options: Get inside, stay inside, stay tuned
items.why: Shelter in the middle of a sturdy building/basement to avoid fallout.

items.prompt: KI after a cesium dirty bomb?
options: No — KI only protects against radioactive iodine
items.why: KI does nothing against cesium; it only blocks thyroid radioiodine uptake.

items.prompt: Alert, afebrile adult: ptosis, double vision, can't swallow, weakness spreading down.
items.why: Descending symmetric flaccid paralysis with a clear mind = botulism.

items.prompt: White powder spilled from a letter onto a clerk's hands.
options: Keep still, isolate area, wash hands with soap & water, call law enforcement/HazMat
items.why: Contain, wash, notify. Prophylaxis only if testing indicates a threat.

items.prompt: Vomiting began 20 minutes after radiation exposure.
